observations: body L1, L25, L30: the dashes after «III.» and before «Caussin» and «Ibn ‘Ezrā» measure 10.0 to 10.2 pt and are transcribed as dashes.
body L2, L6, L9, L15-L17, L19-L20, L23, L32: the dashes of the transliterated names are long dashes (5.2 to 5.5 pt); the name of al-Battānī is divided between L16 and L17 with the dash repeated.
body L29: «fût» is printed for fut.
body L32-L33: no hyphen is printed after «per».

body L11-L14: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIV) add to this page: «Priore II saec. Chr. medietate, Theon Smyrnaeus (minime cum Alexandrino confundendus) annum sideralem, quem a tropico non distinguit, ponit 365 1/4 esse dierum; annum anomalisticum, quo Sol ad apogeum redit, 365 1/2. Motum igitur praecessionis negans, manifeste putat apogeum solare totum zodiacum percurrere 1461 annis, i. e. 27′ 6″ 1/2 quotannis moveri! Unde haec absurda sumpserit nescimus; error in textu Graeco non potest coniici, nam, ut Martin p. 110 animadvertit, auctor ipse addit Solem ad idem altitudinis punctum, id est ad eandem a Terra distantiam, eadem diei hora singulis bienniis redire (1). Recte igitur Martin l. c. iudicat: ‹ Ecce vero Theon Smyrnaeus solaris apogei in zodiaco motum erga aequinoctia et erga stellas iam affirmaverat, et ita quidem iusto citiorem fecerat, ut satius fuerit eum ignorare aut negare, quam talem credere ›. — (1) Theonis Smyrnaei Liber de astronomia, textum edidit, Latine vertit,..... notis illustravit Th. H. Martin, Parisiis 1849, p. 261; Theonis Smyrnaei Expositio rerum mathematicarum ad legendum Platonem utilium, recensuit Ed. Hiller, Lipsiae 1878, p. 172-73.» A whole circle in 1461 years is 14′ 47″ a year.

notes_left L2-L3, L11, notes_right L2-L3: the dashes of «44-45», «89-90», «34-38» and «331-338» measure 2.6 to 4.2 pt, hyphens, and that of «al–Bīrūnī» 4.3 pt, a long dash; «44-45.—» is printed without a space before the dash.
